02 / PAPERS & FORMALIZATIONS

A WORKING COLLECTION / 2026

The math
archive.

Twelve manuscripts. Questions in geometry, combinatorics, and number theory. Browse a first page, read the work here, or take the files with you.

A QUESTION → A CONSTRUCTION → AN ARGUMENT

Showing all 12 papers

PAPER / 01Discrete geometry

Erdős 96 & 977 pages · Manuscript

Unit distances in convex polygons

How many equal-length connections can a convex polygon contain? A collaborative manuscript studies constructions for Erdős problems 96 and 97, with a companion Lean 4 formalization.

With Jensen Kohlmeyer & Liam Price

Download PDF ↓Source files ↓
PAPER / 02Additive number theory

Erdős 148 pages · Draft

Non-unique sums, parts I and II

When integers are written as sums of two elements of a set, how often is the representation unique? This draft studies a quantitative bound addressing both parts of the problem.

With Jensen Kohlmeyer

Download PDF ↓Source files ↓
PAPER / 03Discrete geometry

Erdős 968 pages · Draft

Unit distances in convex position

A separate draft exploring convex point sets with many pairs exactly one unit apart, and a proposed construction challenging a linear upper bound.

With Jensen Kohlmeyer

Download PDF ↓Source files ↓
PAPER / 04Graph theory

Erdős 1088 pages · Draft

Counterexample via arc graphs

An arc-graph construction explores the tension between high chromatic number and restricted subgraphs. The draft proposes a counterexample using triangle-free graphs.

With Jensen Kohlmeyer

Download PDF ↓Source files ↓
PAPER / 05Combinatorics

Erdős 1967 pages · Draft

Permutations avoiding four-term progressions

Can all natural numbers be reordered without creating an increasing or decreasing four-term arithmetic progression? This draft develops a proposed permutation through finite extensions.

With Jensen Kohlmeyer

Download PDF ↓Source files ↓
PAPER / 06Extremal set theory

Erdős 27215 pages · Draft

Arithmetic-intersection families

How large can a family of sets be if every pair intersects in an arithmetic progression? A counting argument investigates the strong variant and its linear error term.

With Jensen Kohlmeyer

Download PDF ↓Source files ↓
PAPER / 07Additive number theory

Erdős 35413 pages · Draft

Two floor-doubling sequences, part I

A study of sums of distinct terms from two floor-doubling sequences. The draft uses binary carries and symbolic systems to investigate the multiplier-two case.

With Jensen Kohlmeyer

Download PDF ↓Source files ↓
PAPER / 08Graph theory

Erdős 94413 pages · Draft

Critical graphs

Graphs that need every vertex, yet resist the removal of edges. A proposed four-color construction studies how vertex-criticality and edge-deletion resilience can coexist.

With Jensen Kohlmeyer

Download PDF ↓Source files ↓
PAPER / 09Additive combinatorics

Green 158 pages · Draft

Lipschitz graphs and progressions

A draft construction of a Lipschitz integer-valued function whose graph avoids nontrivial three-term arithmetic progressions, together with a computational certificate and Lean source.

With Jensen Kohlmeyer

Download PDF ↓Source files ↓
PAPER / 10Coding theory

Green 408 pages · Draft

Binary linear covering codes

How efficiently can binary linear codes cover all nearby vectors? This manuscript investigates covering radius two and a proposed sequence of codes with density approaching one.

With Jensen Kohlmeyer

Download PDF ↓Source files ↓
PAPER / 11Number theory

Green 477 pages · Draft

Quadratic-containment counterexample

A proposed counterexample built from prime squares tests exact containment in a quadratic image. The draft specifically treats exact containment, rather than versions allowing finitely many exceptions.

With Jensen Kohlmeyer

Download PDF ↓Source files ↓
PAPER / 12Additive combinatorics

Green 517 pages · Draft

Binary sumsets at density one half

What structure appears when a set occupies nearly half of a binary vector space? This draft investigates subspaces inside its sumset and quantitative bounds on their codimension.

With Jensen Kohlmeyer

Download PDF ↓Source files ↓

A LITTLE EXPERIMENT

Try the
3n + 1 problem.

Pick a positive integer. If it’s even, halve it. If it’s odd, multiply by three and add one. Keep going.

Does every starting number reach 1?
That’s still an open question.

05 / A LITTLE ABOUT ME

Always
in progress.

I’m Liam. I work across code, mathematics, and creative projects — from making a mathematical argument precise to designing a world you can play in.

I’m interested in how things behave, how they’re made, and how to make them better. This is a collection of the work and the thinking behind it.

Also studying engineering at Purdue University.
